books.section: Topic 5.9 Government Policies During the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Abraham Lincoln, letter to Horace Greeley (August 22, 1862)

stimulus.source_note: Abraham Lincoln, letter to Horace Greeley, August 22, 1862. Public domain. Wording verified against the Collected Works text. “. . .” marks omitted text between passages, quoted in their order in the source.
stimulus.text:
“My paramount object in this struggle is to save the Union, and is not either to save or to destroy slavery. . . . I have here stated my purpose according to my view of official duty; and I intend no modification of my oft-expressed personal wish that all men everywhere could be free.”

—Abraham Lincoln, letter to Horace Greeley, August 22, 1862

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note

rationales.A: Background: Lincoln judges emancipation by whether it saves the Union, not by who supports his reelection.
rationales.C: Background: Lincoln judges emancipation by whether it saves the Union; British recognition is a separate consequence, not his stated test.

rationales.B: Lincoln says he does what he does about slavery because he believes it helps to save the Union, and forbears what he thinks would not help.
rationales.general:
1. Greeley presses Lincoln to act on slavery now, as a moral duty.
2. Lincoln answers with a different yardstick: his official duty to save the Union.
3. Every move about slavery is measured against that one yardstick.
4. His personal wish for freedom is real, but it is not the yardstick he governs by.
Remember: a public letter can state the rule a leader will use before he acts.
